body:
Make global configuration possible for some options and easier for the other.

Some of the idea of what its config fields:

- `job = { threads: int, timeout: int }`. `job.threads` is the number of parallel threads to use (currently twice the number of CPU threads). `job.timeout` is a timeout for any async operation in milliseconds (currently 30000).

- `add = { <the structure of opts in vim.pack.add()> }`. This allows setting default value of options in `vim.pack.add()` in a forward compatible way. Also see #34770. Counter-point is that the same can be achieved by writing custom wrapper around `vim.pack.add()`, but I think it is worth adding here.

    NOTE: This assumes that there will be something like `opts.default_version` to allow to set it to `vim.version.range('*')` which would prefer latest tag release instead of default branch. If not, it might be part of `vim.pack.config()` directly.

comment_data.body:
This looks low-priority to me. Need to wait until there are stronger use-cases.

In any case let's consider using real options, not another `foo.config` thing if possible.

> This looks low-priority to me. Need to wait until there are stronger use-cases.

For providing global default config value - fair. This is also meant to allow configuring something that is not possible to configure now. But yeah, not very urgent.

> Need to wait until there are stronger use-cases.

Just wanted to bump up the use-case for #36078 here since not being able to configure lockfile location makes `vim.pack` unusable for config directories managed via nix as the directory is readonly so vim.pack.add errors out while trying to write to it.

Should this be configured though a function? Are there any other native nvim apis that are configured like that? I'd assume the more consistent option would be something like a `vim.pack.config = {...}` table, no?

> Should this be configured though a function? Are there any other native nvim apis that are configured like that?

Yes, `:h vim.diagnostic.config()`. Using function is more versatile as it allows to validate input before applying to actual config.

> not being able to configure lockfile location makes `vim.pack` unusable for config directories managed via nix as the directory is readonly

That might be a strong reason to change the *default* location. Though https://github.com/neovim/neovim/issues/36078#issuecomment-3381198362 makes a good point:

> If you use a full nix config, you are not supposed to use vim.pack anyway :)

@justinmk 
> That might be a strong reason to change the _default_ location. Though [#36078 (comment)](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/issues/36078#issuecomment-3381198362) makes a good point:
> 
> > If you use a full nix config, you are not supposed to use vim.pack anyway :)

unless you want to keep your nix and non-nix neovim configs identical. 
id prefer to not have to maintain multiple copies of effectively the same config.

Another idea I've had (after ever relevant news about bad packages) is something along the lines of a `cooldown_period` option. This will allow to control how much time should have passed for a revision to be allowed during `vim.pack.update()`.

> control how much time should have passed for a revision to be allowed

But an attacker can easily set the commit-date.
I'd like this to accept a setup function like lazy's `config` & only run it if the plugin is actually used (I don't need rust plugins when editing python code)

@vulns-are-features-too that should be the responsibility of the plugin author, not yours. But if the plugin doesn't do it properly, you can just only load it in an `ftplugin` file to run in a specific filetype

It'd be nice to be able to change a few git options in `vim.pack.Spec` (e.g. whether to fetch/checkout submodules).

An example is https://gitlab.com/HiPhish/rainbow-delimiters.nvim, where the author discourages users to clone its submodules, since they're only used in testing. At the moment, `vim.pack` clones all plugins with their submodules recursively.

> It'd be nice to be able to change a few git options in `vim.pack.Spec` (e.g. whether to fetch/checkout submodules).

This is outside of scope for this issue, which is about global `vim.pack` config.

And I am fairly strongly against adding a new plugin specification field for how `git` fetching works.

> ... where the author discourages users to clone its submodules, since they're only used in testing

This is a quote from the README:

> They are just used for development and won't cause any harm, they will just bloat your setup.

It looks like it is harmless to clone all submodules, while being a conscious decision to use submodules even though they are not needed for users. For development it is possible to manually manage them separately.

@justinmk, I'd like an update+pointers as to how to proceed here.

I still think that a function `vim.pack.config()` is the better approach than a set of options. Here are the main reasons:

- Makes it possible to use functions, userdata (timers or whatnot), and tables with metadata as option values.

- Naturally localized config only for `vim.pack`. Like I can see how some options may become more general (e.g. "number of job threads") and having two "real" options for general and `vim.pack` specific is too much. Instead it can be that `vim.pack` inherits default from global "real" option but `vim.pack.config` allows adjusting for `vim.pack` only.

- More discoverable documentation (all in one place).

- Easier implementation (although this is a one time investment per new option).

- It is a documented [dev pattern](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/a5aa62e37b82214a1d4d1e0a54d193b155fb340c/runtime/doc/dev.txt#L412-L414).

As far as I can tell, the only benefit of using real options is that it makes `vim.pack` feel more built-in.

---

Here is a list of configurations that I currently think are reasonable:

- Not possible to configure now:
    - Lockfile location - string with path, may contain environment variables (like `$XDG_DATA_HOME/nvim`). Probably also allow empty string to not use lockfile, but that might be tricky.
    - Number of job threads - number of parallel threads to use (currently twice the number of CPU threads).
    - Job timeout - number of milliseconds before stopping any async operation (currently 30000).

- Quality of life improvements:
    - Default `opts` for `vim.pack.add`, `vim.pack.update`, and `vim.pack.del`. This is possible to achieve via custom wrapper, but might still be worth adding.

If the "real option" path is still preferable, I'd need guidance for their names and shapes. With `vim.pack.config` I'd go with:

```lua
vim.pack.config({
  lockfile = vim.fs.joinpath(vim.fn.stdpath('config'), 'nvim-pack-lock.json'),
  job_threads = 2 * (uv.available_parallelism() or 1),
  job_timeout = 30000,
})
```

> As far as I can tell, the only benefit of using real options is that it makes `vim.pack` feel more built-in.

There are numerous benefits (I'll add this to `:help dev`):

- scopes: global/buf/win/tab (with ability to "graduate" from one to the other later)
- `OptionSet` event
- completion
- UI: `:verbose set ...`, `:options`, etc.

IOW, it's an options system :) something we don't get for every bespoke `foo.config`.

lockfile/job_threads are really poor reasons to rush this.

p.s. @lewis6991 has a PR https://github.com/neovim/neovim/pull/31280 for supporting Lua funcs on options, that should help. (It may need a small revisit after https://github.com/neovim/neovim/pull/39849 )

> * scopes: global/buf/win/tab (with ability to "graduate" from one to the other later)

I have my doubts that this will ever be useful for `vim.pack`.

> * completion

The in-buffer completion requires set up LSP, in which case completion would work for both `vim.o` and `vim.pack.config()` argument. The completion for command line - yeah.

> * `OptionSet` event
> ...
> * UI: `:verbose set ...`, `:options`, etc.

These are good points, yeah.

> IOW, it's an options system :) something we don't get for every bespoke `foo.config`.
> 
> lockfile/job_threads are really poor reasons to rush this.

Sure, if you say so.

---

So what is the current direction? Should these be `'packlockpath'`, `'packthreads'`, `'packtimeout'` global options? Or a single `'packopt'` dict-style similar to `'diffopt'`? Or a combination of both: `'packlockpath'` and `'packjob'`?

> So what is the current direction? Should these be `'packlockpath'`, `'packthreads'`, `'packtimeout'` global options? Or a single `'packopt'` dict-style similar to `'diffopt'`? Or a combination of both: `'packlockpath'` and `'packjob'`?

I don't know of any guidance on that yet :) Judgement is needed.

- re 'packtimeout':  I think it's a cop-out to expect users to fiddle with timeout options, and I would prefer that we have a global way to "stop all current tasks".
- re 'packthreads': there is no reason for this to be configurable.

> * re 'packtimeout':  I think it's a cop-out to expect users to fiddle with timeout options, and I would prefer that we have a global way to "stop all current tasks".

Although good in theory, I don't think there are any plans or even concrete ideas about how to make this work. My vague understanding is that this would require either hard-coding `<C-c>` as a mapping, tweaking `vim._async`, both, or even more. Probably not something I'm comfortable with doing.

In turn, increasing timeout for async operations is a valid use case for people with slow Internet connection. There was increase of the used value (#36992) to a reasonably high number, but configuring it is still something I'd consider as needed.

> * re 'packthreads': there is no reason for this to be configurable.

I can see this being useful either to increase parallel jobs on capable machines (where default `2 * (uv.available_parallelism() or 1)` falls short) or decreasing on old machines. Out of three, this is indeed has the least priority.

---

I'll start with `'packlockpath'` then, as it seems to be in demand. I am open to adding both of the above also, if there is a change of heart.

---

As this issue was created specifically to discuss `vim.pack.config`, I think I'll close this as resolved: it is not welcome and native options should be preferred. Each one is better tracked in its own issue (like #36078 for future `'packlockpath'`).

> increasing timeout for async operations is a valid use case for people with slow Internet connection

and what happens if they want to cancel it?

> > increasing timeout for async operations is a valid use case for people with slow Internet connection
> 
> and what happens if they want to cancel it?

They wait until it is finished or force close the Neovim outside of it, I guess :)

Once again, I am not against "universal `<C-c>` to cancel any ongoing operation". It's just that I don't see a good (i.e. robust and not problematic for users+plugins) way to implement this. While adjustable timeout aligns nicely with other timeout-based options, is easy to implement in `vim.pack`, is easy to understand for users of `vim.pack`.

> just that I don't see a good (i.e. robust and not problematic for users+plugins) way to implement this.

There is a clear path, which is for `vim.system` to be integrated with the jobs system. https://github.com/neovim/neovim/issues/39552 (Plugins that use `vim.uv` directly, have opted-out of that, and have chosen to provide a worse experience.)

> While adjustable timeout aligns nicely with other timeout-based options, is easy to implement in `vim.pack`, is easy to understand for users of `vim.pack`.

It's not blocked if people really want it. But it's a temporary mitigation.
